newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hopes Hong Kong will keep civil liberties.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hopes Hong Kong will keep civil liberties.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday that Hong Kong might be of much less value to China if the civil liberties of the island's people were crushed.

"I'm not so sure that it can exist with all of its potential to help China modernise its own economy and open opportunities for its own people, if the civil liberties of the people are crushed," Clinton told a news conference. "So I think it would be wrong on its own merits, but I think it might wind up being less useful to China."

"So I would hope very much that they would look for ways to maximize the continuation not only of the economic system but of the personal freedoms that the people of Hong Kong have enjoyed in making it such an economic engine," Clinton said.
Separately, Clinton also strongly defended his policy of "constructive engagement" with China.

"I still believe, over the long run, being engaged with China, working with them where we can agree...and continuing to be honest and forthright and insistent where we disagree, has the greatest likelihood of having a positive impact on China," Clinton said.

"I believe that the impulses of the society and the nature of the economic changes will work together, along with the availability of information from the outside world, to increase the spirit of liberty over time," Clinton added. "I don't think that there's any way that anyone who disagrees with that in China can hold that back. I just think it's inevitable, just as the Berlin Wall fell."
